name: Heterotic M-Theory Domain Wall
description: Two flat walls with three dimensions of space at the ends of the interval of heterotic M-theory, found by André Lukas, Burt A. Ovrut, Kellogg S. Stelle, and Daniel Waldram in 1999. Between the walls the metric scales with powers of a function $H$ linear in the coordinate $y$ along the interval, the volume of the Calabi-Yau space scales as $H^3$, and our universe is the worldvolume of one wall.
convention: The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$, and $\delta$ is the Dirac delta. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: In the eleven dimensional theory of Petr Hořava and Edward Witten, an observer near either end of the eleventh dimension sees supergravity on a half space, with an $E_8$ gauge field on its boundary [horava1996heterotic]. They proposed that the $E_8\times E_8$ heterotic string at strong coupling is M-theory on $\mathbb{R}^{10}\times S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$, an interval whose two ends are planes of ten dimensions, and that anomalies require 248 vector multiplets, one copy of $E_8$, on each end [horava1996heterotic]. The interval grows with the string coupling, and in 1996 they fixed the gauge coupling on its ends in terms of the gravitational one [horava1996heterotic, horava1996eleven]. Witten compactified six of the remaining ten dimensions on a Calabi-Yau space in February 1996 and found that the 4-form field of M-theory cannot vanish there, since the ends of the interval are magnetic sources for it [witten1996strong]. To first order the volume of the Calabi-Yau space then changes linearly along the interval, and with the gauge coupling on one end held fixed, the coupling on the other end diverges at a finite length, where that volume reaches zero [witten1996strong]. With the couplings matched to their measured values the interval is longer than the Calabi-Yau space is wide, so between the two scales the universe has five dimensions [witten1996strong, lukas1999universe].¶André Lukas, Burt A. Ovrut, Kellogg S. Stelle, and Daniel Waldram reduced the theory to those five dimensions, keeping a part of the 4-form along the Calabi-Yau space that cannot be set to zero [lukas1999universe]. Their theory is a gauged $N = 1$ supergravity with a potential proportional to $\alpha^2/V^2$ for the volume $V$ of the Calabi-Yau space, and terms of opposite sign on the two ends, all set by one constant $\alpha$ of the Calabi-Yau data [lukas1999universe]. Flat space does not solve it, and they found in its place a pair of flat walls with three dimensions of space, $ds^2 = a_0^2H\,\eta_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu + b_0^2H^4dy^2$ with $H = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\alpha|y| + c_0$, $V = b_0H^3$, and constants $a_0$, $b_0$, and $c_0$ [lukas1999universe]. The coordinate $y$ runs from $-\pi\rho$ to $\pi\rho$ with its ends identified and $y \to -y$ as a symmetry, so its fixed points $y = 0$ and $y = \pi\rho$ are the walls, where the slope of $H$ changes sign [lukas1999universe]. The solution keeps four of the eight supercharges, solves the five dimensional theory in full, and to first order in $\alpha$ is Witten's deformed Calabi-Yau background [lukas1999universe]. Our four dimensions are the worldvolume of one wall, and in the words Lukas, Ovrut, and Waldram used again, "the Universe lives on the worldvolume of a three-brane" [lukas1999universe, lukas1999cosmological].¶Away from its sources $H$ is linear, and Lukas, Ovrut, Stelle, and Waldram noted that it could be glued from any number of pieces with slopes $\pm\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\alpha$, each change of slope a wall of its own [lukas1999universe]. M5-branes wrapped on curves of the Calabi-Yau space are such walls in the bulk, allowed to move along the interval [khoury2001ekpyrotic]. The volume $V$ grows toward one wall and shrinks toward the other, and where $H$ reaches zero the geometry has a curvature singularity [khoury2001ekpyrotic]. Mirjam Cvetič and Max Wiesner put the hidden wall at that point in 2024, where its $E_8$ coupling diverges and the warp factor $a_0^2H$ falls to zero, and found that instantons of M5-branes wrapping the Calabi-Yau space keep the warp factor finite [cvetic2024nonperturbative]. The wall that remains has finite curvature and stays strongly coupled [cvetic2024nonperturbative]. Cvetič and Wiesner found the corrections in closed form with a K3 surface and a torus in place of the Calabi-Yau space, and the wall then continues to a supersymmetric anti-de Sitter vacuum, a thick variant of the single wall of Lisa Randall and Raman Sundrum [cvetic2026smooth].¶Lukas, Ovrut, and Waldram then set the walls moving, keeping the profile in $y$ rigid while the size of the walls, the distance between them, and the volume of the Calabi-Yau space change with time [lukas1999cosmological]. In comoving time $t$ the walls scale as $|t - t_0|^p$ and the interval as $|t - t_0|^q$, with $p = \frac{3}{11}\left(1 \mp \frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}\right)$ and $q = \frac{2}{11}\left(1 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\right)$, the rolling radii of weakly coupled heterotic string theory [lukas1999cosmological]. Each solution begins or ends at a curvature singularity at $t = t_0$, and in the one they said "perhaps corresponds most closely to our notion of the early universe" the walls expand after it while the interval shrinks [lukas1999cosmological]. Andrew Chamblin and Harvey Reall found in 1999 a static bulk with a constant $M$ that holds the wall at rest for $M = 0$; for $M > 0$ the walls move, some in what they called the "pair creation" or annihilation of a universe and its shadow [chamblin1999dynamic].¶Justin Khoury, Ovrut, Paul J. Steinhardt, and Neil Turok proposed in 2001 that the hot big bang began on this wall [khoury2001ekpyrotic]. A light third wall, an M5-brane that may separate from the hidden wall, drifts slowly across the interval and strikes ours, and the collision fills our wall with hot radiation and matter [khoury2001ekpyrotic]. Khoury, Ovrut, Steinhardt, and Turok named it the ekpyrotic universe, after the conflagration of Stoic cosmology that consumes the universe and reconstitutes it [khoury2001ekpyrotic]. Fluctuations of the moving wall leave a nearly scale invariant spectrum of density perturbations with no inflation, and gravitational waves with a strongly blue spectrum [khoury2001ekpyrotic]. Jean-Luc Lehners, Paul McFadden, and Neil Turok found in 2007 the solution in which the walls collide, unique if the curvature stays finite as they approach, and showed that the earlier cosmological solutions are portions of it [lehners2007colliding].¶Mario Reig and Ignacio Ruiz asked whether the interval could be the dark dimension of micron size tied to the dark energy, and found from the lifetime of the proton that it is at most of order $10^{-28}$ m [reig2026dark]. With the warping of Lukas, Ovrut, Stelle, and Waldram the length is bounded by the point where the Calabi-Yau space on the hidden wall shrinks to zero volume, an effect Ralph Blumenhagen and Antonia Paraskevopoulou called "lethal" for an interval of micron size [reig2026dark, blumenhagen2026towards]. Blumenhagen and Paraskevopoulou proposed in May 2026 to cancel the tadpole on each wall separately, so that the volume of the Calabi-Yau space is the same along the whole interval and the interval is a plain product with that space [blumenhagen2026towards]. Approximate symmetries of baryon and lepton number, left by abelian factors on the walls, could then suppress the decay of the proton [blumenhagen2026towards].

related.text: Two flat walls at the ends of a fifth dimension as well, with anti-de Sitter space between them. With quantum corrections, and a K3 surface and a torus in place of the Calabi-Yau space, Cvetič and Wiesner found the heterotic wall continuing to anti-de Sitter space, a thick version of Randall and Sundrum's single wall [cvetic2026smooth].

A thin wall with flat space on either side, which accelerates as a bubble. The heterotic walls stay flat and at rest, held there by a potential for the volume of the Calabi-Yau space [lukas1999universe].

A wall in anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions moving past a black hole, which those on it see as an expanding universe. The heterotic walls move too, rigidly, their size and separation following powers of time [lukas1999cosmological].

Walls of scalar field in gauged supergravity of five dimensions, there between regions of anti-de Sitter space. In the heterotic wall the scalar is the volume of the Calabi-Yau space, with a potential that falls as the inverse square of that volume [lukas1999universe].
Universes confined to a wall or a vortex in more dimensions, the first brane universes [khoury2001ekpyrotic].
Another beginning for the big bang from string theory, from an almost empty vacuum that then deflates faster than light [khoury2001ekpyrotic].

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3, y)$, with $t$ having dimensions of time, $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ lengths along the walls, and $y$ a length across the interval, with $\mathrm{sgn}(y)$ its sign. The points $y$ and $-y$ are one point, and we take $|y| < \pi\rho$, away from the wall at $y = \pm\pi\rho$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ is the derivative of $ct$.
